title: compact cross-language streaming resilience + credential-throttle tuning (TS/Go/Py parity)
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes: Small ergonomic API changes to the TS streaming client, parity fixes for credential throttling across Go/Python SDKs, and default retry-window tuning. No breaking changes for existing call sites.
description:
Summary: This PR harmonizes a lightweight credential-throttle (reauth backoff) across the TypeScript, Go, and Python SDKs and adds a compact streaming resilience surface to the TS SDK so calling code can opt into connection-level fallbacks without pulling in heavyweight session machinery. Motivation: In high-concurrency server scenarios we observed auth storms where token refreshes triggered reconnect cascades; the goal here is an ergonomic default that reduces thundering reauths and provides parity for streaming ergonomics across SDKs.

What changed (high level):
- TypeScript: introduced StreamController API (opt-in) that centralizes reconnect/backoff + graceful resume. Exposes .pause(), .resume(), .on('fallback', cb).
- Cross-SDK: added credential-throttle window config (default 10s) to prevent concurrent refresh attempts for the same credential id. Implemented in TS and mirrored in Go/Py helpers.
- Retry tuning: default backoff profiles tightened for small-token workloads (reduce tail latency under steady load).
- Tests & docs: unit + integration tests for throttle behavior; updated SDK changelogs and a short migration note.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-2029) [x] unit tests added [x] integration smoke test against the canary runtime [x] docs/migration note [x] changelog entry

Commits (summary):
- a7f3b22 add StreamController: compact API for pause/resume and fallback hook; initial tests
- c1d9f88 implement credential-throttle and backoff profiles; cross-sdk spec updates
- e3b9a07 docs: migration note, changelog, and test flakiness fixes

Files changed (high level):
- packages/sdk-ts/src/stream/controller.ts (new) -- 120 LOC core controller with internal state machine
- packages/sdk-ts/src/stream/index.ts (expose new API surface)
- packages/sdk-ts/tests/stream/credential-throttle.test.ts (new)
- packages/common/auth/credential_throttle.ts (shared spec + TS impl)
- packages/sdk-go/internal/cred/throttle.go (mirror implementation)
- packages/sdk-python/redwood/cred/throttle.py (mirror implementation)
- docs/sdk/migration/ts-stream-controller.md (migration notes)
- examples/ts/stream-resume-sample.ts (usage snippet)

Small TS usage example (illustrative):
const controller = client.streamController({ credentialId: 'svc-12', throttleWindowMs: 10000 });
const s = controller.openChat({ model: 'redwood-compact' });
s.on('fallback', (meta) => console.warn('fallback to polling', meta));
await s.start();
// caller can pause/resume during backoffs

Review conversation (high level and truncated):
- Sofia Martinez (reviewer): "Nice compact surface. Please prefer explicit naming for the 'fallback' event payload and document lifecycle edge cases (server-initiated close vs network blip). Also suggest adding a short integration test that simulates concurrent refreshes."
- Arjun (author): "Addressed: renamed payload to { reason, previousState }, added integration test that spawns 8 concurrent clients sharing a credential id; added comments explaining server-initiated close semantics."
- Lukas Weber (reviewer): "LGTM modulo a small comment on the backoff constants; prefer exponential capped at 5s for initial window."
- Arjun: "Adjusted profile to cap at 5s per Lukas + updated changelog to call out the tuning."
- Maya Chen (approver): Approved after CI green and integration run stable.

CI and checks:
- lint (TS): pass
- unit tests (TS): pass
- integration tests (TS-canary): initially one flaky failure (stream-resume-sample) -> rerun -> pass
- go unit tests (cred throttle): pass
- python unit tests (cred throttle): pass
- cross-sdk smoke: pass

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: callers relying on undocumented streaming internals might behave differently if they depend on implicit reconnect semantics. Mitigation: StreamController is opt-in; default client behavior unchanged. Added migration doc and examples.
- Risk: throttle misconfiguration could delay legitimate refreshes. Mitigation: default window conservative (10s) and opt-out via config.

Merge strategy: squash and merge. Reasoning: small set of cohesive commits; simplifies git history.

Post-merge actions:
- cut minor patch on TS SDK (v1.7.3) with migration note (handled by release pipeline)
- announce in #sdk-updates with example snippet and recommended config for high-concurrency servers

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the TS API minimal — the goal is parity-level ergonomics without pushing session lease semantics into the default surface. Follow-ups planned to: (1) expose metrics hooks for throttling events, (2) add a lightweight CLI diagnostic for credential storms, (3) measure real-world impact on Dedicated capacity customers.
